"A storm is coming" could refer to several things:

Literal weather — A storm system approaching your area.

Pop culture references:
 Hans Zimmer track from The Dark Knight Rises soundtrack (2012) — a short, ominous instrumental piece[1]
 Tommee Profitt & Liv Ash song — dramatic cinematic track with lyrics about an inescapable storm[2][3]
 2017 documentary "A Storm Is Coming: Learning the Blues with Coney Island Pete" about blues musician Peter Collins[4]
 Narrative trope — TV Tropes catalogs this as a classic foreshadowing device signaling impending trouble[5]

Linguistic note — The phrase is often used metaphorically for any looming crisis, not just weather. As discussed on Reddit, it functions more as a presentmoment observation of imminent arrival than a future prediction.[6]

Which did you mean — actual weather, one of the songs/films, or the metaphorical usage?
